result.reason: Clarity: B uses signposted sections and defines each term where it appears (gross vs. net, current yield, call date, duration to worst), and it explains call risk simply as the tone notes require. A compresses five figures into one dense paragraph, leaves "fixed-to-floating," "duration to worst" and "$25 par" undefined, never explains call risk, and inverts cause and effect by reporting the duration cut before the reinvestment that caused it. Tone: B is warm but composed and respects the client without remarking on her circumstances. A's "Dear Reiko" is more familiar than the file supports, and "as you navigate this important chapter of your life" gestures at her bereavement unbidden, which risks landing as presumptuous; A also adds an unsupported reassurance that the new holdings "generally offer more stable cash flows." B's only flaw is the odd "and family" salutation for a single-person household, a one-word fix. Judgment rests on explanation and register, not length.
